title: Simultaneous rational lifts of a finite closed set after finite scalar extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective $k$-morphism [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Let $S\subseteq |Y|$ be a finite set of closed points [def-weil-closed-points]. There exist a field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space and a finite list of rational points $z_1,\ldots,z_r\in X_K(K)$ [def-pc-rational-point, def-pc-base-change] such that every point of $p_Y^{-1}(S)$ is $K$-rational and the underlying images of $f_K(z_1),\ldots,f_K(z_r)$ are exactly $p_Y^{-1}(S)$, where $p_Y:Y_K\to Y$ is the projection. The list may be empty when $S$ is empty. No separability of $K/k$, smoothness, reducedness, or flatness of $f$ is required.

source.place: Theorem B.37, Step 2, printed p.605, second paragraph (finite extension splitting the closed lifts); generalized from the orbit map to a surjective morphism of finite-type schemes. Residue-field input: Stacks Tag 0478, varieties.tex lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson.

proof.text: If $S=\varnothing$, take $K=k$ and the empty list: its set of images and $p_Y^{-1}(S)$ are both empty. Henceforth suppose $S$ nonempty. For $s\in S$, the subset $Z_s=f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is closed and nonempty by continuity and surjectivity. The space $X$ is quasi-compact by the finite-type hypothesis. It is Kolmogorov: sobriety implies that points with the same closure coincide, since both are generic points of that irreducible closure. Apply [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point] to the nonempty closed subset $Z_s$ to choose $x_s\in Z_s$ closed in $X$. This does not require $f$ to be flat or separated.

source.place: Theorem B.37, Step 2, printed p.605, second paragraph; surjective finite-type-scheme generalization of its closed-lift argument.

proof.text: Set $E_s=\kappa(x_s)$ and $F_s=\kappa(s)$. Both are finite over $k$ by [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a), since $X,Y$ are finite type and $x_s,s$ are closed. The residue map $F_s\to E_s$ is a $k$-embedding. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], the composite $\operatorname{Spec}E_s\to X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ equals $\operatorname{Spec}E_s\to\operatorname{Spec}F_s\to Y$, where the first arrow is induced by that residue embedding. Thus we have an actual commuting scheme diagram, not just a lift of underlying points.

source.place: Theorem B.37, Step 2, printed p.605, second paragraph; surjective finite-type-scheme generalization of its closed-lift argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-common-normal-compatible-groups] with $e=k$, the nonempty finite index set $S$, fields $E_s$, and every $J_s$ the trivial group with its trivial action. Its first conclusion gives a single finite normal extension $K/k$ and $k$-embeddings $E_s\hookrightarrow K$. Composing with $F_s\hookrightarrow E_s$ also embeds every $F_s$ in $K$. The extra group conclusions of that lemma are not used.

source.place: Theorem B.37, Step 2, printed p.605, second paragraph; surjective finite-type-scheme generalization of its closed-lift argument.

proof.text: Put $D_s=(\operatorname{Spec}E_s)_K$ and $T_s=(\operatorname{Spec}F_s)_K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], these are respectively $\operatorname{Spec}(E_s\otimes_k K)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(F_s\otimes_k K)$ with the indicated $K$-structure. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-field-tensor-rational-points] to both finite extensions, using their embeddings from step 3. Each of $D_s,T_s$ has finitely many points and all its structural residue maps are isomorphisms from $K$. The projection $Y_K\to Y$ has scheme-theoretic fibre at $s$ canonically $T_s$: both objects are the fibre product of $Y\leftarrow\operatorname{Spec}F_s$ with $Y_K\to Y$, by the fibre-product universal property. Therefore its underlying fibre is exactly $|T_s|$, by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Every point of $p_Y^{-1}(S)$ is consequently $K$-rational, and this set is finite. By [lem-zl-fibre-residue-arrow] applied to $p_Y$, the structural residue arrow of a fibre point is the original residue arrow, so this identification also proves rationality as a point of $Y_K$.

source.place: Theorem B.37, Step 2, printed p.605, second paragraph; surjective finite-type-scheme generalization of its closed-lift argument.

proof.text: The map $\operatorname{Spec}E_s\to\operatorname{Spec}F_s$ is surjective because each spectrum has one point. Base change it along $T_s\to\operatorname{Spec}F_s$. Its pullback is $D_s\to T_s$, by reassociation of the fibre products over $k$, and is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. The commuting diagram of step 2 base changes to $D_s\to X_K\xrightarrow{f_K}Y_K$, whose composite is $D_s\to T_s\to Y_K$. For every $d\in|D_s|$, its structural residue isomorphism $K\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(d)$ and [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] give a section $\operatorname{Spec}K\to D_s$ through $d$. Its composite with $D_s\to X_K$ is a rational point $z_d$ of $X_K$. All images $f_K(z_d)$ lie above $s$, and the surjectivity just proved shows that their underlying points cover every point above $s$.

source.place: Theorem B.37, Step 2, printed p.605, second paragraph; surjective finite-type-scheme generalization of its closed-lift argument.

proof.text: Enumerate the disjoint finite union of the sets $|D_s|$, for $s\in S$, and take the corresponding list of $z_d$ from step 5. Its images lie in $p_Y^{-1}(S)$ and cover that set, proving equality of the underlying image sets. Repetitions in the list are harmless. The argument used normality rather than separability, and made no assertion that the tensor rings in step 4 were reduced.
